page: Microsoft Azure D2ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDSv5 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, configured with 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The system includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided by a bundled 77 GB SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. It operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor with an x86_64 architecture.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1889.99 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1581.0, both falling into the average range. However, multi-core and memory subsystem performance are limited. The stress-ng multi-core score of 1932.99 and Geekbench multi-core score of 1866.0 are positioned in the lower tier. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read-only bandwidth at 14.72 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 13.46 GB/sec.

Given its hardware profile, the D2ds_v5 offers a cost-effective entry point for workloads that do not require high parallel processing power or massive memory bandwidth. The primary tradeoff is the low multi-core scaling and constrained memory throughput, which limits its utility for heavy database operations or complex multi-threaded tasks. It is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, basic single-threaded applications, small-scale web serving, and simple utility tasks that benefit from dedicated CPU allocation and local SSD storage.
